claims.claim: We call the day after today 'tomorrow' because it is the day after the day before, which is called 'yesterday.'
claims.note: Tomorrow is the day after today, not the day after yesterday (the day before).

claims.claim: The word 'tomorrow' comes from the Latin word 'tumor,' which means 'future.'
claims.note: The word 'tomorrow' comes from Old English roots, not the Latin word 'tumor' (which means swelling).

claims.claim: Your heart is the supercomputer of your body
claims.note: The heart is a muscular pump, not a supercomputer; the brain functions as the supercomputer of the body.

claims.claim: It pumps blood throughout your entire body
It carries oxygen and nutrients to all your organs
It keeps your brain and muscles functioning at full speed
Your heart is also responsible for regulating your blood pressure
It keeps your heart rate steady
Things move.
Things talk.
Things sometimes make noise.
Toy cars help other things.
Toy cars are fun to play with.
Scientists study how things move, how they heat up, and how things break down.
Scientists learn about how plants grow and how animals hunt for food.
Science helps us solve real-life problems like how to make a better toy or how to keep our homes safe.
Scientists and astronomers study the length of months because it helps them predict seasons, measure time, and study how the Earth rotates around the Sun.
Some months are actually shorter because they are closer to the Sun, which means they get more sunlight and heat.
claims.note: Month lengths are not determined by distance to the Sun. Earth's distance to the Sun varies due to its elliptical orbit, but this causes seasons, not the differing lengths of months in the calendar.

claims.claim: Other months are longer because they are farther away from the Sun, which means they get less heat and less light.
claims.note: Month lengths are unrelated to being farther away from the Sun; the number of days in a month is historical and based on calendar design.

claims.claim: Electric cars have special batteries that run on electricity instead of gas.
Electric cars do not need oil or gas to run.
Electric cars are much better for the environment.
Electric cars can travel long distances on one charge.
Electric cars are a great way to help reduce pollution and save money on fuel.
Planes use special engines and wings to fly.
Planes fly because they have to travel high up where the air is thinner and cooler so they can go faster.
claims.note: Planes do not fly primarily to go faster in thin air; they fly high to avoid weather and terrain and for fuel efficiency.

claims.claim: Planes need to fly over mountains and oceans to get to all the places they need to go.
The biggest planet is Jupiter.
Jupiter is so big because it has lots of gas and ice in its huge cloud tops.
claims.note: Jupiter's size is due to its total mass formed from accumulating gas and dust in the early solar system, not because of ice in its cloud tops.

claims.claim: Rhythm is how things happen in time, like when you tap your foot to the music.
claims.note: Tapping your foot to music is typically keeping the beat, not the rhythm.

claims.claim: Beats are the steady, repeating notes that make music sound smooth and steady.
claims.note: Beats are a steady pulse, though describing them as repeating notes is a slight oversimplification.

claims.claim: A drum beat is a steady beat that keeps the music moving forward.
Trains use a special type of track called a metro, which is designed to run on a fixed path.
claims.note: A metro is a rapid transit system or subway, not a type of track, and all standard trains run on fixed tracks.

claims.claim: The train can't move backward, which is why they have to travel in one direction.
claims.note: Trains are fully capable of moving backward.

claims.claim: The trains themselves are also long because they need room to store all their equipment and passengers.
A pumpkin is usually orange or yellow
A pumpkin grows in the fall
Singing in the shower helps get rid of all the tension and makes you feel relaxed.
Vocal cords are like little microphones that help us sing better.
claims.note: Vocal cords are muscular folds in the larynx that vibrate to produce sound, not microphones.

claims.claim: We eat berries because they are full of yummy juices
Berries are like tiny superfoods
Berries give us energy to run and play
Berries taste great
New Year's is celebrated on January 1st because it is the first day of the year.
The year is also known as the Gregorian calendar.
claims.note: A year is a unit of time, not the calendar itself.

claims.claim: The Julian calendar was used before the 15th century.
The Julian calendar didn't have a leap year.
claims.note: The Julian calendar did include leap years every four years.

claims.claim: We had to add an extra month every four years to keep track of time in the Julian calendar.
claims.note: The Julian calendar added an extra day, not an extra month, in leap years.

claims.claim: Ice floats because it is made up of tiny, invisible water droplets called ice crystals.
claims.note: Ice is not made of invisible droplets, and ice crystals are generally visible.

claims.claim: These tiny ice crystals are super light and float because they have a lot of kinetic energy.
claims.note: Ice floats due to lower density caused by molecular spacing, not high kinetic energy; in fact, freezing water has lower kinetic energy than liquid water.

claims.claim: Kinetic energy means they are moving fast enough to overcome the pull of gravity.
claims.note: Molecules in a solid ice crystal are locked in place and do not have the high kinetic energy required to overcome gravity.

claims.claim: Turning off lights and electronics when you leave a room reduces your carbon footprint.
Carpooling, walking, or biking instead of driving alone reduces your carbon footprint.
Using energy-efficient light bulbs and washing clothes with cold water instead of hot reduces energy use and carbon emissions.
Using reusable bags reduces paper usage.
claims.note: Reusable bags are typically used to replace single-use plastic or paper bags, but reusable bags themselves are not made of paper, making the phrasing confusing or factually imprecise.

claims.claim: Choosing products made from recycled materials or with low packaging waste helps reduce environmental impact.
Turning off the air conditioning when you leave a room saves energy.
Trees absorb carbon dioxide.
A banana tastes sweet.
A banana tastes juicy.
claims.note: Bananas are starchy and not typically considered juicy fruits like oranges or melons.

claims.claim: A banana has a little bit of a sour taste, like when you bite into a lemon.
claims.note: Bananas do not taste sour or like lemons.

claims.claim: Friends share your interests.
Friends help you with your problems.
Friends make you laugh.
When you are with friends, you feel safe.
You know that friends care about you.
Friends give you the courage to try new things and be yourself.
Having a budget helps you manage your money wisely.
It stops you from overspending on things you don't really need, like clothes or gadgets.
It makes sure you have enough money for things like school, travel, and fun activities.
It teaches you how to save money and build good financial habits.
Being afraid of the dark is totally normal.
Fear of the dark is caused by your brain trying to keep you safe.
As you grow older, your brain learns that the darkness is safe.
Galaxies are mostly made up of hot, glowing gas and dust.
claims.note: Galaxies are mostly made of dark matter, not gas and dust.

claims.claim: Hot, glowing gas and dust are what makes galaxies look blue and glow in the night sky.
claims.note: Galaxies glow primarily because of the combined light of billions of stars, not just gas and dust.

claims.claim: The gas is mostly made up of hydrogen and helium.
The dust is made up of tiny particles like silicon, carbon, and oxygen.
Galaxies are full of superhot stars, which give off their own light and heat.
If you mix blue and yellow, it will be a bright color like rainbow.
claims.note: Mixing blue and yellow makes green, not a rainbow of colors.

claims.claim: You can mix red and green to make a green-blue color.
claims.note: Mixing red and green typically creates a muddy brown or neutral color, not green-blue.

claims.claim: You can mix orange and purple to make a purple-orange color.
claims.note: Mixing orange and purple typically creates a brownish, muted neutral color rather than a distinct purple-orange combination.

claims.claim: Flowers smell sweet.
Flowers give us color.
Flowers can be red, yellow, or purple.
Food can get spicy due to heat traveling up the food chain, starting with the plants that grow it.
claims.note: Spiciness is caused by chemical compounds like capsaicin produced by plants, not by heat traveling up the food chain.

claims.claim: As plants grow, they release chemicals called terpenes and flavonoids, which give them their smell and taste.
claims.note: Terpenes and flavonoids are indeed chemicals responsible for many plants' smells and tastes, though they are not the primary cause of chili pepper spiciness.

claims.claim: When we eat the food, our mouths get hot from the spicy flavor, and our taste buds pick up the heat.
claims.note: Spiciness is not a taste picked up by taste buds, but a sensation of heat and pain triggered by chemical activation of pain receptors on the tongue.

claims.claim: Our brains process the heat and send signals to our nervous system, making us feel excited or even a little bit scared.
claims.note: The brain processes pain and temperature signals from capsaicin, which can trigger physiological responses associated with excitement or mild distress.

claims.claim: Allergies happen when your immune system mistakes harmless things like pollen, dust, or even food like peanuts, as if they were a big, dangerous threat.
When you react to these things, your body releases chemicals and tiny white blood cells called leukocytes to fight off the invaders.
Sometimes, those immune cells get a little bit too excited, and they attack your own tissues instead.
claims.note: Allergies are an overreaction to harmless foreign substances, not typically an autoimmune attack on one's own tissues.

claims.claim: Allergies can make your throat feel scratchy or itchy, your nose run, or even cause you to have a hive or a rash.
Butterflies fly because they have long, thin wings.
Butterflies can't walk on the ground like us.
claims.note: Butterflies do have legs and can walk on surfaces, even though they primarily fly.

claims.claim: Butterflies use their wings to help them travel.
We have day and night because our bodies need different amounts of light and darkness to help us feel safe and healthy.
claims.note: Day and night are caused by the Earth's rotation on its axis, not by human biological needs.

claims.claim: Day is when the sun shines brightest, giving us energy and warmth.
Night is when the sun goes down, and we sleep.
claims.note: While the sun goes down at night, not everyone sleeps during the night due to different time zones and work schedules.

claims.claim: It's like our bodies are trying to tell us when it's time to rest and restore energy.
Rainbows happen because of the way light travels through water
When it rains, the drops of water hit the air and bump into each other, making tiny bumps in the air
claims.note: Raindrops do not create tiny bumps in the air by bumping into each other.

claims.claim: These bumps are like tiny mirrors, reflecting the colors of the rainbow right back at you
claims.note: Water drops act as prisms that refract and reflect light to form rainbows, not as tiny bumps in the air acting as mirrors.

claims.claim: Food can smell funny because of the way the food is cooked or how it's stored.
If you eat something that has been sitting in the refrigerator for a while, it might have a strong smell of chlorine from the water.
claims.note: Chlorine from tap water is not a standard reason for stored food developing a strong or funny smell in a refrigerator.

claims.claim: Some foods smell funny because they are raw or have just been cut.
The smell of food is usually gone when you eat it.
claims.note: Much of the flavor we experience while eating actually comes from aromas traveling up into our nose (retronasal olfaction), so the smell is very much present while eating.
